subject.title: [Feature]: Decompose embedded attempt runner into execution phases

question: Should the embedded attempt runner be decomposed as one coordinated phase refactor, or should maintainers sponsor a sequence of smaller invariant-focused extractions?
rationale: The work is behavior-preserving but large and central; phase ownership and sequencing materially affect reviewability, conflict rate, and regression exposure, so the protected item needs maintainer sponsorship.

options.title: Stage invariant-first extractions
options.body: Extract setup and prompting, stream settlement, and finalization through separate focused PRs with independent behavioral proof.

options.title: Land one coordinated refactor
options.body: Implement all phase boundaries in one large PR with broad parity tests and explicit lifecycle-invariant review.

options.title: Defer the refactor
options.body: Continue with smaller local helpers until current feature churn subsides, accepting the ongoing review and conflict cost.

recommendation.title: Stage invariant-first extractions
recommendation.body: Extract setup and prompting, stream settlement, and finalization through separate focused PRs with independent behavioral proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person opened the focused item and has the strongest recent history across the central runner and adjacent runtime refactors.
